extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of literature; poets, literary students, critics, and those interested in the relation of literature to American democracy
extracted.subtask_description: Whitman's reflective essayistic guidance on what makes poetry and national literature valuable: qualities to aim for in verse, how books should be judged, and the role of native literature in shaping American democracy and morals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of Longfellow's poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Longfellow is eminent in the poetical style and forms of the present age; he brings what is dearest to the human heart and taste, is the poet of melody, courtesy, deference, sympathetic gentleness, and a universal poet of women and young people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitman praises poetry that soothes and heals, that is vital with flavor, motion, and grace; not revolutionary or offensively new, not singing exceptional passions but striking a splendid average. Example anti-pattern: poetry that deals in jagged escapades or harsh blows. Notes mention his translations and their high quality ('said to be better than the vernaculars').

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's emotional ground and movement
rubrics_metrics.description: In youth and maturity poems are charged with sunshine; as soul takes precedence the dusk becomes the poet's atmosphere — the play of Imagination with sensuous objects of Nature for symbols and Faith makes up a poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic creation should use sensuous nature as symbol and let imagination, love, and pride be the unseen impetus. Advice: poets increasingly favor half-lights and evening moods with age; the poem is a chess-game of these forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final literary tests lie in Nature, not technical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The last deciding tests applicable to a book are entirely outside of technical and grammatical ones; any truly first-class production has little or nothing to do with the rules and calibres of ordinary critics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitman advocates judging books by 'Nature' — the ocean, daylight, mountain, forest — as if some disembodied human soul gives its verdict. Practical implication: authenticity, outdoor freshness, and resonance with nature supersede formal correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to poetic meaning and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Common teachers/critics always ask 'What does it mean?' but grand poetic passages are to be taken at free removes; much of a poem is what is not gathered and perhaps the main thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers and critics should allow for elusive, evocative meaning rather than demanding explicit intellectual definition. Grand passages are experienced 'off one side' rather than by direct, literal analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic reading stance: put reader in rapport
rubrics_metrics.description: To a poetic student Whitman: 'I only seek to put you in rapport. Your own brain, heart, evolution, must not only understand the matter, but largely supply it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional: students must actively supply their own sensibilities; the poem is a collaborative stimulus, not a fully explicit deposit. Anti-pattern: relying solely on the poem to do all explanatory work for the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve immediacy and outdoor flavor in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman resisted smoothing or over-editing notes taken outdoors; he printed from impromptu notes, 'hardly even the seasons group'd together,' fearing to drop what 'smack of outdoors or sun or starlight might cling to the lines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical production advice: avoid over-polishing to preserve immediacy, freshness, and the sense of having been in Nature. He admits this risks technical errors but values authentic 'specimen-days' over technical neatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry's form: take passages at 'free removes' like stars
rubrics_metrics.description: Grandest poetic passages are only to be taken at free removes, as we sometimes look for stars at night, not by gazing directly toward them, but off one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stylistic criterion: subtle indirectness and oblique approach often produce the strongest poetic effect. Anti-pattern: literal, direct illumination of every image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature as the moral and social formative power
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman asserts that the great literature penetrates all, shapes aggregates and individuals, and constructs, sustains, or demolishes social forms; literature will be the ultimate instrument to meet social and religious problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for writers: aim for works that can influence manners, religion, education, law, and public character. Example historical claim: a single great poem or literatus may change society as much as wars or dynasties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for an original American literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy can never prove itself until it founds and luxuriantly grows its own forms of art, poems, schools, theology—native authors and literatuses expressing democracy and the modern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescription for producers and cultural planners: create native imaginative literature (especially poetry) that is original and suited to American conditions; such literature should permeate the nation and produce teachers and moral character. Anti-pattern: reliance on imported literary forms without native adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature should produce national identity and moral substratum
rubrics_metrics.description: What will make the western world a superior nationality must be vigorous literatures, perfect personalities and sociologies, original and transcendental—forming a religious and moral character beneath political and productive bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to generate archetypal poems, heroes, and common narratives that knit diverse states and peoples into a moral unity. Practical goal: literature that radiates and begets appropriate teachers, schools, manners, and a 'fervid IDEA' binding the nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative literature is the primary need
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman privileges imaginative literature (especially poetry) as the 'stock of all' and as the main field requiring original native development in America; science and journalism may flourish, but imaginative, spinal and essential attributes are lacking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For writers and critics: prioritize imaginative originality and 'spinal' (core) qualities over technical or journalistic excellence when assessing cultural health. Note: literature dominates other arts for moral influence in modern civilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy's moral health requires contact with Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: American Democracy most of all affiliates with the open air, is sunny and hardy and sane only with Nature—regular contact with outdoor light and air and growths is required or democracy will dwindle and pale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural prescription: encourage nature-based practices and representations in literature and education as a health-element and beauty-element underpinning politics, sanity, religion and art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity over conventional critical metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitman contends that true literary value is not measured by critics' technical rules ('the bloodless chalk of Allibone's Dictionary') but by authenticity, emotional truth, and responsiveness to nature and human feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation guidance: give precedence to works' authentic emotional power and natural vivacity rather than strict adherence to conventional critical metrics. Accept some technical errors if the work's veracity and glints of life remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the literatus as priest/teacher
rubrics_metrics.description: The priest departs; the divine literatus comes—what the republic needs now is the poet or great literatus of the modern to act as teacher, moral shaper, and national expresser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation for literary producers: take on responsibilities beyond art for moral and social leadership; craft works that can instruct, inspire, and shape national belief. This is a prescriptive standard for the social role of writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility about claims of originality in young literatures
rubrics_metrics.description: On the charge of want of racy nativity and special originality Whitman says America must first be 'well saturated with the originality of others' and respectfully consider heroes before Agamemnon before it can be worthily original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for literary development: value assimilation and saturation of existing traditions before demanding abrupt, naive originality; historical grounding and respect for predecessors are important steps toward true originality.
